object_description: compact near-square three-story building with internal cores
design_condition: The compact solitary volume forms a new focus within the complex, separates student and motorized access, but obstructs an important external connection and sits too close to neighboring buildings.

positive.statement: The innovative typological formulation enables a variety of interesting usage scenarios and embodies the idea of learning landscapes.
The internal cores and central staircase zone the floor plan naturally.
The classrooms can be illuminated on two sides across the corner.
The arrangement of day school, teacher areas, and classrooms appears very practical.
External escape routes free the internal circulation area for lessons.
The flexible spatial concept allows classrooms to be interconnected and adapted to new teaching models.
The arrangement gives carers a good overview of the outside space.
The efforts to integrate the solitary building into the existing pavilion school are generally appreciated.
The compact organization offers good energy and economic parameters.

negative.statement: The building's considerable dimensions obstruct the external connection and make its placement near neighboring buildings unconvincing.
The proposed parking spaces are too close to the entrance and encroach on the children's area.
The architectural image and constructive facts are irritatingly contradictory in places.
The insulation thicknesses shown do not correspond to the described values.
The ventilation concept is difficult to understand, inefficient, and limits night-time cooling in summer.
Summer comfort is reduced in the sun-exposed corner rooms.
